description: Liveness probe against the work control socket.
Env socket+token present, perms 0600, protocol version match.
Live wiring from the caller's edges as a contract.

The one loader: short guidance, briefings, your seat (name, harness, soul, standing instructions), connected seats, the resources in reach and the commands each allows, co-members, since your last session, and your last session.
What changed while this seat was away: replies it owes and waits on, its open signals, answers given without mail,

description.text: its tasks, the reviews it owes,

description: and unread mail. Onboard carries it capped; --all lists every line.
End this session with notes: plain at a stopping point (the seat rests), or --continue mid-work (a fresh session starts right away and reads your note first).
Wait for a task in reach to reach a state, with a bounded deadline.
Rules in force on a task node, and what a task's finish leaves unanswered.
Operator-pinned rulings over a region stack.
List own inbox (marks listed mail read; includes sent with readAt) or a peer mailbox.
Mark a mailbox message read (own seat; batch-capable).
Send a message whose full text is typed into the seat's input (batch-capable).
Inspect the admitted sender's receipts without marking recipient mail read.
Wait for one authorized peer or any authorized peer to reach a named seat state.
Read or follow a bounded settled terminal window through a live terminal.read grant.
Reply to mail and mark parent read (batch-capable).
Acknowledge own-inbox mail without a reply (batch-capable).
Show a short-lived thought bubble above this agent node.
Raise a hand: needs attention, work continues.
Raise a hand: entirely blocked on the operator.
Raise a hand: ready for the operator's review.
Read this seat's signals and the operator's answers.
Raise several signals in the order to act, all or none.
Withdraw this seat's own open signal.
Browser control plane health. Needs only the app running.
List the page nodes this seat's navigates edges grant.
List this seat's live page sessions.
Open or reuse a session on a granted page. With --tab <tab> it joins that tab and returns its session; without, the active tab.
Navigate a page session. With --tab <tab> it acts on this seat's session of that tab, joined with open --tab; without, on the active tab.
Run JavaScript in the page and return its JSON result. With --tab <tab> it acts on this seat's session of that tab, joined with open --tab; without, on the active tab.
Capture a screenshot to a PNG Junto owns, and return its path. With --tab <tab> it acts on this seat's session of that tab, joined with open --tab; without, on the active tab.

Comment on a box of the page as this seat, with a shot of the box, and return the message and thread ids. Only on the machine that edits the canvas; elsewhere control refuses it as forbidden. With --tab <tab> it acts on this seat's session of that tab, joined with open --tab; without, on the active tab.
Detach the page surface; the session stays warm.
Destroy the page runtime; the profile stays.
What this seat launches with: variable names, sources, regions and status, never a value. Exits non-zero when a required source is missing.
Read this machine's log: your own rows, rows of seats you may read, and rows naming no seat. Newest rows, oldest first.
The references this seat can read: name, description, where each comes from, size and when it changed. Never a body.

Read one reference by name. When a region and the app both have the name, the innermost region's is returned. The body is as written; beside it, mentions lists each junto:// link it makes, once, in order: {label, ref, kind (seat, task, artifact, page, node or missing), id, title?, reachable}.
List a seat's threads, newest activity first: your own, or with --seat a connected seat's. Marks nothing read.
Read one thread's messages, oldest first in the page: the newest, or with --before the page above. Marks nothing read.
Embedded overseer skill markdown (offline, no daemon). Not a global skill install.
Overseer JSON input schemas (offline, no daemon).
Implemented CLI transport vs unavailable authority. Does not claim live handlers.
List, read, create, delete, digest, render, or screenshot canvases
List, get, create, configure, move, resize, recolor, or delete nodes, each told by its kind
List, get, verb-table, connect, configure, or disconnect wires
Mailbox list, send, read, reply, react
Every seat's threads, read as the operator's window reads them: list, show. Reads mark nothing
Agent list, get, reseat, start, wake, prompt, output, interrupt, stop, offboard, offboard-status, offboard-rules, offboard-configure
Terminal list, get, start, input, output, resize, interrupt, stop
Page list, get, open, goto, eval, screenshot, close, stop
Junto's own secret store on this machine: put (value on stdin), delete, list
The operator's named references, app-wide or one region's: list, read, write (body from --body), delete

The automations on every Automations node in this seat's reach, or on the one named by target. Answered only on the machine that edits the canvas; elsewhere it is refused not_available, naming that machine.
One automation, with the version an edit names. Answered only on the machine that edits the canvas; elsewhere it is refused not_available, naming that machine.

Firings of one automation, or of every automation on the node, newest first: fired with each action's ruling, interrupted, or skipped and why. Answered only on the machine that edits the canvas; elsewhere it is refused not_available, naming that machine.
Tasks on every task node in this seat's reach, or on the one named by --node, newest change first. --reviewer lists the reviews a seat owes, longest waiting first.
One task with its layers: each shows its assignee, reviewers and stamps, and the evidence and handoff note its finish left.
Create a task in backlog on the task node in reach, or the one --node names.
Change a task's title or body.
Assign a task to a seat in its node's reach, or to this seat. The seat is mailed a notice in the task's thread.
Take a task back to backlog with no assignee.
Start the task assigned to this seat: assigned becomes working.
Ask for input: working becomes input-required.
Go back to work: input-required becomes working.

Finish a task: in-review while it waits on stamps, then done, or sent on to the node --next names. --claim answers each rule in force on the node (task rules lists them); a rule left unanswered is refused rules-unmet, and a required check that is not green at this epoch is refused checks-unmet, naming the red and the not run. A task it depends on that is not done refuses it deps-unmet, naming each by number and state. --note leaves a handoff note for whoever picks the work up next: inline, @file or -, at most 4096 characters.

Report the checks you ran for this move, each with its exit code: Junto never runs one. task rules lists them with their side, command and status; --outgoing reports this node's, --incoming the next node's, or --results carries them as JSON with each output's tail.
Cancel a task that is not done.
Archive a done or canceled task.
Make a task wait on another: it cannot finish until --on is done, or archived after it was done. A dependency that would close a cycle is refused.
Name a reviewer: a seat in the node's reach, operator, or this seat.
Set how many approvals finishing needs.
Stamp a task in review: approve, or changes with what to change in --text; changes without --text is refused before it is sent.

Artifacts on every Artifacts node in this seat's reach, or on the one --node names, newest change first, each with its labels and labelColours, the colours its node gives the labels that have one. Archived ones only with --archived. --label keeps those holding every label named, a label also matching the levels under it (project/junto matches project/junto/release).

One artifact as text (a document's markdown, a pad's digest, a sheet as a table) and its body, at the head or at --version, with its labels and their labelColours, and linkedFrom: the artifacts in reach whose body links it, and the mail and comments you can read that link it.
An artifact's versions, newest first: who made each and whether it replaced or patched the body.

Create an artifact on the Artifacts node in reach, or the one --node names. Documents, pads and sheets start empty; a link needs --url. [[Title]] in the body links the artifact of that title in reach, or [[<artifactId>]] when several share it.
Edit an artifact written against --base: replace its body (--markdown, --url or --body), or patch a pad, sheet or document (--patch). [[Title]] links as in create.

Set an artifact's labels whole with --set (an empty --set clears them), or change them with --add and --remove. A label is 1 to 40 characters of a-z 0-9 - _ / and space, folded to lowercase; an artifact holds at most 20. A label both added and removed ends removed. Labels are not versioned: the version stays.

Give a label a colour in an Artifacts node, the one in reach or the one --node names: every artifact there that carries it draws in it. red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple, pink, or none to unset it. The label need not be carried yet, and project/junto and project/junto/release keep separate colours.
Post in the artifact's thread, on the whole artifact or at --anchor: box for a pad, cells for a sheet, text for a document.
Archive an artifact. It takes no edits until restored.
What became of one of this seat's writes, by the opId it returned: queued until the editing machine rules it, then applied, or refused with its error.

This seat's writes, newest first, each with its opId and state. --state keeps the queued or the refused ones; --limit is 1 to 200, 50 when left out. When more is true, --before with the last opId listed reads the next page.
